confidence_notes: I based the restaurant, coffee and beer anchors on web searches of crowd-sourced cost-of-living aggregators (Numbeo, Citycost and MyLifeElsewhere). These put a mid-range meal for two at about INR 750-765, a draft beer at about INR 150, a cappuccino at about USD 1.5-1.6 and a cheap meal at about USD 1.7-2.4. One aggregator page showed an outlier meal price, which I left out. I raised the mid-range meal and the inexpensive meal a little to allow for July 2026 prices and venues popular with tourists. I converted rupees at about 88-90 INR per USD. The cocktail anchor uses one crowd-sourced Expatistan figure of about INR 326 for a club cocktail, raised to allow for typical hotel-bar and restaurant prices. I found no reliable price for a glass of wine. That figure is estimated from a bottle price of about INR 1,050 and the usual price gap between beer and wine in Indian bars, so it is low confidence. Drinks are also uncertain because few places in Varanasi serve alcohol and many are hotel bars. All accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not searches of live listings. They reflect July, the monsoon low season, when riverside guesthouses near the ghats may cut prices or have their access limited by flooding.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink anchors follow the Varanasi aggregator data, cross-checked against other mid-sized cities in North India such as Agra and Lucknow and the budget-traveller hubs of Rishikesh and Jaipur. Accommodation follows typical budget hostel chains and the pattern of guesthouses and three-star hotels in Indian pilgrimage and tourist cities.
